Research focus: Dynamic placement of edge-AI application tasks
Method: Containerized video pipeline with frame extraction, parallel object-detection services, and frame combination
Workload or data: Video object detection; varies video quality and detection-container count
Hardware and network assumptions: Reported deployment uses Raspberry Pi for frame extraction and MacBook Pro and Asus systems for detection services; Kubernetes cluster
Verified finding: More detection containers reduce processing time up to a workload-dependent threshold; beyond it, processing time can increase
Limitation or scope caution: One application and deployment; video quality affects processing time and communication between services
Relevance to this project: Motivates measuring both parallel processing benefit and inter-stage communication cost

Method: Survey and taxonomy covering AI for edge and AI on edge
Hardware and network assumptions: No single experimental hardware or network setup
Verified finding: Organizes edge-intelligence goals, architectures, and research challenges
Limitation or scope caution: Survey conclusions depend on the literature and scope reviewed; it is not a new benchmark
Relevance to this project: Provides conceptual framework and terminology, not an experimental baseline

Research focus: Distributed CNN inference across heterogeneous edge devices
Method: DistrEdge uses deep reinforcement learning to select model partitioning and device assignments
Workload or data: CNN inference with variation in device types and network bandwidth
Hardware and network assumptions: Experiments include embedded NVIDIA Jetson devices and varied Wi-Fi bandwidth; memory constraint is not modeled
Evaluation metrics: Images per second, latency, speedup against baseline methods
Verified finding: Reports 1.1--3x speedup over the best-performing baseline in evaluated cases
Limitation or scope caution: Results depend on tested models, devices, network conditions, and baselines; memory constraints are excluded
Relevance to this project: Candidate inference approach; future tests should include memory and communication costs

Method: Federated averaging aggregates locally computed model updates
Workload or data: Five model architectures and four datasets, including unbalanced and non-IID data settings
Hardware and network assumptions: Mobile clients motivate the method; detailed hardware and network assumptions require full-text extraction
Evaluation metrics: Communication rounds relative to synchronized stochastic gradient descent
Verified finding: Reports 10--100x fewer communication rounds in the evaluated settings
Limitation or scope caution: Training result tied to the evaluated models, datasets, and comparison baseline; not a distributed-inference result
Relevance to this project: Provides a primary federated-training baseline and illustrates communication cost

Method: Review of IoT, edge intelligence, 5G, and blockchain integration in autonomous vehicles
Workload or data: Autonomous-vehicle systems and related technology integration
Hardware and network assumptions: Literature review; no single experimental hardware or network setup
Verified finding: Reviews technology integration, associated challenges, and research directions for autonomous-vehicle systems
Limitation or scope caution: Review evidence rather than a prototype benchmark; claims should not be treated as measured performance
Relevance to this project: Provides application context for vehicle--edge--cloud collaboration and vehicle safety, security, and reliability considerations

Research focus: Federated learning for connected and automated vehicles
Method: Survey of centralized and decentralized FL frameworks, vehicle data sources, applications, and privacy/security methods
Workload or data: Connected and automated vehicle model training; reviews application datasets
Hardware and network assumptions: Survey; no single hardware or network configuration
Evaluation metrics: Literature synthesis of FL applications, datasets, and challenges
Verified finding: Identifies FL use cases and discusses privacy, communication overhead, heterogeneity, and security challenges
Limitation or scope caution: Survey findings; not a new cooperative-perception or system performance experiment
Relevance to this project: Secondary model-training context; distinguishes federated training from online cooperative perception

Research focus: V2X cooperative 3D object perception with heterogeneous agents
Method: Vision Transformer using heterogeneous multi-agent self-attention and multi-scale window attention
Workload or data: LiDAR 3D object detection on simulated V2XSet, generated using CARLA and OpenCDA
Hardware and network assumptions: Simulation; reported training on Tesla V100; agent communication radius 70 m
Evaluation metrics: 3D detection average precision under baseline and noisy settings
Verified finding: Authors report 21.2% AP gain over single-agent baseline and at least 7.3% over compared intermediate-fusion approaches
Limitation or scope caution: Simulation-to-reality generalization, scalability, privacy, and adversarial robustness remain concerns
Relevance to this project: Supports multi-agent fusion; motivates checking pose, timing, agent heterogeneity, and real network constraints

Method: Spatial confidence maps select sparse, perceptually critical feature regions and adapt sharing to bandwidth
Workload or data: Camera/LiDAR and vehicle/drone scenarios on OPV2V, V2X-Sim, DAIR-V2X, and CoPerception-UAVs
Hardware and network assumptions: Dataset and simulation evaluations; real wireless deployment not established
Evaluation metrics: 3D detection AP at IoU 0.50/0.70 and communication volume in bytes
Verified finding: Authors report improved perception/communication trade-off; on OPV2V report over 100000x lower communication volume than selected baselines while outperforming them
Limitation or scope caution: Benchmark- and protocol-specific; spatial selection does not fully address temporal communication scheduling
Relevance to this project: Directly informs joint evaluation of communicated bytes, latency, and perception quality

Research focus: Open benchmark for V2V cooperative perception
Method: CARLA/OpenCDA simulated dataset and benchmark comparing early, late, and intermediate fusion, including Attentive Intermediate Fusion
Workload or data: 73 simulated scenes, 11464 frames, and 232913 annotated 3D vehicle boxes
Hardware and network assumptions: CARLA/OpenCDA co-simulation; not a physical vehicle radio test
Evaluation metrics: Benchmark compares LiDAR fusion strategies and detection performance
Verified finding: Provides reproducible simulated V2V data; physical-world transfer and real network reliability are not established
Limitation or scope caution: Dataset suitable as a candidate for multi-agent configuration C, subject to resource and licensing checks

Research focus: Cooperative BEV semantic segmentation and multi-agent perception
Method: Sparse fused axial attention aggregates multi-view camera features across agents
Workload or data: Cooperative BEV segmentation on OPV2V; extensions to single-agent multi-camera segmentation and multi-agent LiDAR 3D detection
Hardware and network assumptions: Dataset-based evaluation; no deployed vehicle V2X stack
Verified finding: Benchmark performance does not establish real-world wireless or vehicle deployment behavior
Limitation or scope caution: Alternative cooperative fusion architecture and task for evaluating multi-agent perception

Research focus: V2X cooperative perception methods and open challenges
Method: Survey of collaboration strategies, agent selection, data alignment, feature fusion, and uncertainty
Workload or data: Review of vehicle-to-everything cooperative perception research
Hardware and network assumptions: Literature survey; no single hardware/network benchmark
Verified finding: Highlights communication delay/data loss, agent and model heterogeneity, and uncertain perception as open challenges
Limitation or scope caution: Survey rather than new experimental evidence
Relevance to this project: Supports the project's requirements for link reliability, freshness, alignment, and local fallback
